description: Issue-area knowledge schema for retail and commercial lease analysis. Defines expected coverage, applicability gating, exposure statements, caution signals, and negative-space clues.
notes: v1.1: Added applicability gating. v1.1.1: Removed bare 'security' from LP-04 activation_clues. v1.1.2: LP-12 activation_clues tightened to prevent false positives on default/remedies language. v1.1.3: LP-14 extended with partial-abatement expected_element and 'wholly untenantable only' unfavorable-pattern detection. v1.1.4: LP-13 covered_unfavorable extended to detect materially asymmetric mutual indemnification (per cross-model audit 2026-04-28). LP-11 rule precedence clarified between covered_unfavorable and potentially_unenforceable per same audit. v1.1.5: exposure_statement field on LP-02, LP-03, LP-08, LP-10, LP-12, LP-17 extended from string to object with tenant/landlord/neutral perspective variants. v1.2.0: Added LP-19 Utilities (required), LP-20 Exclusivity (conditional, extracted from LP-05), LP-21 Guaranty of Lease (conditional, promoted from discovered_provision_patterns). LP-05 expected_elements updated: removed 'exclusive use right scope' (now LP-20's responsibility); related_issue_areas updated to include LP-20. discovered_provision_patterns updated: removed 'Guaranty' pattern (now LP-21). v1.3.0: Added LP-22 SNDA, LP-23 Percentage Rent, LP-24 Damage & Destruction, LP-25 Condemnation/Eminent Domain, LP-26 Quiet Enjoyment, LP-27 Landlord Default & Tenant Remedies, LP-28 Compliance with Laws, LP-29 Right of Entry/Landlord Access, LP-30 Estoppel Certificate, LP-31 Co-Tenancy, LP-32 Hazardous Materials. Promoted SNDA, Percentage Rent, Co-Tenancy, and Hazardous Materials from discovered_provision_patterns. Schema now covers 32 issue areas per CAM_Schema_Selection_Methodology.md.

coverage_states.covered: Provision present and consistent with standard form
coverage_states.covered_unfavorable: Present but materially one-sided against tenant
coverage_states.partial: Some expected elements present, others missing or weakened
coverage_states.ambiguous: Present but interpretation-dependent; practical effect unclear
coverage_states.missing: Issue area expected in this lease but provision is absent
coverage_states.broken_xref: Provision references a section, exhibit, or defined term not found in the document
coverage_states.potentially_unenforceable: Structural or legal defect that may limit enforceability
coverage_states.review_needed: Insufficient evidence to assert a state; surface for human judgment
coverage_states.not_applicable: Issue area does not apply to this lease based on exclusion clues or document type
coverage_states.applicability_unclear: Cannot determine whether this issue area should be present; needs human judgment

applicability_levels.required: Expected in every retail/commercial lease of this type
applicability_levels.conditional: Expected only when specific indicators are present in the document
applicability_levels.optional: May or may not be present; absence is not a concern without other signals

caution_signal_definitions.common_dispute_area: Frequently litigated provision type; outcome heavily fact-dependent
caution_signal_definitions.governing_law_sensitive: Practical effect varies significantly by jurisdiction
caution_signal_definitions.landlord_leverage_point: Landlord typically holds stronger enforcement position if disputed
caution_signal_definitions.tenant_leverage_point: Tenant holds strong position; landlord enforcement limited
caution_signal_definitions.potentially_unenforceable: Known structural defect or clause pattern with enforceability concerns
caution_signal_definitions.cascade_risk: Change to this provision may silently affect other provisions via cross-reference

issue_areas.name: Rent & Payment Terms
expected_elements: base rent amount or formula
payment due date (day of month)
late payment fee or penalty mechanism
grace period for late payment
accepted payment methods
additional rent definition (what constitutes additional rent)

coverage_state_rules.missing: No rent provision found in document
coverage_state_rules.partial: Base rent defined but late fee, due date, or additional rent definition absent
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: References rent schedule or exhibit not present in document
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Late fee grace period removed or shortened below 5 days

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: No enforceable rent obligation; landlord has no clear basis for payment demand or default notice
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Tenant's payment obligation and enforcement timeline undefined; creates ambiguity in default proceedings
negative_space_clues: Section marked 'Reserved' or 'Intentionally Omitted'
Reference to 'Exhibit A — Rent Schedule' with no Exhibit A attached
Blank dollar amount placeholder not filled in
common_tenant_modifications: Grace period extensions (5 days → 10 days)
Reduced late fee percentage
Removal of additional rent catch-all definition

issue_areas.name: Rent Escalation
issue_areas.notes: Absence may be intentional (flat-rent leases).
expected_elements: annual increase mechanism (fixed percentage or CPI)
escalation cap or ceiling
effective date of first escalation
calculation methodology

coverage_state_rules.missing: No escalation provision found and no flat-rent exclusion language present
coverage_state_rules.partial: Escalation mechanism defined but cap or calculation method absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: CPI reference present but index not specified
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: No cap on CPI increases
coverage_state_rules.not_applicable: Document explicitly states rent is fixed for the full term

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Rent frozen at initial amount for entire term; landlord loses inflation protection

exposure_statement.tenant: No rent escalation cap; tenant bears uncapped exposure to inflation-driven rent increases over the lease term
exposure_statement.landlord: No rent escalation cap; landlord retains pricing flexibility but bears the dispute risk that comes with uncapped or formula-driven increases
exposure_statement.neutral: Rent escalation lacks a cap or fully defined calculation methodology; future rent increases may become disputed or difficult to price over the lease term

negative_space_clues: Escalation section header present but body blank or marked Reserved
Cross-reference to CPI index definition absent from Definitions article
common_tenant_modifications: CPI cap addition (e.g. maximum 3% per year)
Fixed-percentage substituted for uncapped CPI
First escalation deferred one year

issue_areas.name: Lease Term & Renewal
expected_elements: initial term duration
commencement date or conditions
expiration date
renewal option count and duration
renewal notice period and deadline
rent at renewal (formula or fair market value mechanism)

coverage_state_rules.missing: No term provision found
coverage_state_rules.partial: Term defined but renewal options, notice periods, or renewal rent mechanism absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Renewal at 'fair market value' with no determination mechanism defined
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: References commencement conditions defined in Work Letter or exhibit not present
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Renewal notice period unusually short (under 90 days)

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Lease duration undefined; tenancy may be at-will or interpreted as month-to-month

exposure_statement.tenant: Term and renewal rights unclear; tenant may lose right to remain in premises or face holdover penalties
exposure_statement.landlord: Renewal mechanism undefined; landlord faces uncertainty over future occupancy and has weakened leverage to reset rent or terms at expiration
exposure_statement.neutral: Lease term and renewal rights are incompletely defined; the absence of a renewal rent mechanism leaves both occupancy continuity and pricing unresolved at expiration

negative_space_clues: Renewal option section header with body struck or marked Reserved
Reference to 'Option to Renew' in Table of Contents but section absent from body
common_tenant_modifications: Extended notice period for renewal (90 days → 12 months)
Added renewal options (1 → 2 or 3)
Capped renewal rent at fixed percentage over expiring rent

issue_areas.name: Security Deposit
issue_areas.notes: Bare 'security' removed from activation_clues v1.1.1 — too broad.
expected_elements: deposit amount
return deadline after lease expiration
permitted deduction conditions
interest obligation (if any)
letter of credit alternative conditions

coverage_state_rules.missing: Deposit referenced in lease header or recitals but no deposit provision found
coverage_state_rules.partial: Amount defined but return timeline or deduction conditions absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Return deadline unusually long (over 60 days)
coverage_state_rules.not_applicable: No deposit references found anywhere in document

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: If deposit was negotiated, landlord has no documented security mechanism
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Deposit obligation referenced but terms undefined; return and deduction rights unprotected
negative_space_clues: Deposit amount shown as blank or $0.00 in lease summary
Letter of credit alternative referenced but terms not defined
common_tenant_modifications: Reduced deposit amount
Burn-down schedule (deposit reduces over time)
Shortened return deadline

issue_areas.name: Permitted Use
issue_areas.notes: Cascade risk: force majeure definition changes can alter continuous operation obligations.
expected_elements: specific permitted use description
continuous operation obligation
prohibited use restrictions
co-tenancy or anchor dependency language

coverage_state_rules.missing: No permitted use provision
coverage_state_rules.partial: Use defined but continuous operation, prohibited use restrictions, or co-tenancy language absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Use defined broadly without specific business description
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Permitted use cross-references definition not present in document
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Continuous operation obligation present with no force majeure carve-out

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: No restriction on how tenant uses space; may conflict with other tenant exclusives in the center
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Use restrictions absent or undefined; tenant may face exclusive use violations or continuous operation penalties
negative_space_clues: Exclusive use clause header present but body blank
Reference to 'Exhibit B — Exclusive Use Area' with no exhibit attached
common_tenant_modifications: Broadened permitted use description
Weakened continuous operation obligation (shall → may)
Added co-tenancy condition tied to anchor tenant

issue_areas.name: Maintenance & Repairs
expected_elements: tenant maintenance obligations (interior, non-structural)
landlord maintenance obligations (structural, roof, exterior)
HVAC responsibility allocation
repair response time obligations
damage and destruction repair process

coverage_state_rules.missing: No maintenance allocation provision
coverage_state_rules.partial: General allocation present but HVAC, structural, or response times absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Tenant bears HVAC replacement cost with no age or condition cap
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: HVAC responsibility stated as 'shared' without clear allocation formula

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Maintenance obligations default to tenant under many jurisdictions
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Maintenance allocation undefined; tenant may bear unexpected capital repair costs including structural and HVAC replacement
negative_space_clues: HVAC section header present but body struck or blank
Landlord repair obligation section marked Reserved
common_tenant_modifications: Landlord bears HVAC replacement cost above threshold amount
Structural repair obligation shifted to landlord

issue_areas.name: Common Area Maintenance (CAM)
issue_areas.notes: Not applicable in gross or full-service leases.
expected_elements: tenant's proportionate share calculation method
included expense categories
excluded expense categories
annual CAM increase cap
tenant audit rights
reconciliation timeline

coverage_state_rules.missing: CAM references present in lease but no CAM provision found
coverage_state_rules.partial: Share calculation present but exclusions, cap, or audit rights absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: No annual CAM cap; audit rights absent or time-limited to 30 days
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Proportionate share defined by landlord's reasonable determination with no formula
coverage_state_rules.not_applicable: Gross or full-service lease structure confirmed

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Tenant may owe undefined share of all building operating expenses with no audit protection
issue_areas.exposure_statement: CAM exposure uncapped and unauditable; tenant cannot verify or challenge operating expense pass-throughs
negative_space_clues: CAM cap provision header present but percentage blank
Audit rights section marked Reserved or Intentionally Omitted
Excluded expenses list cross-references exhibit not attached
common_tenant_modifications: 5% annual CAM increase cap added
Capital expenditure exclusion added
Management fee cap (typically 15% of operating expenses)

issue_areas.name: Insurance Requirements
expected_elements: tenant commercial general liability minimum ($1M per occurrence, $2M aggregate standard)
property insurance obligation
business interruption coverage
landlord as additional insured
certificate of insurance delivery obligation
waiver of subrogation

coverage_state_rules.missing: No insurance provision
coverage_state_rules.partial: Liability minimum present but additional insured, property coverage, or waiver of subrogation absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Coverage minimums unusually high; waiver of subrogation absent
coverage_state_rules.potentially_unenforceable: Named insured requirement conflicts with standard policy structure

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Tenant may operate uninsured; landlord has no recourse against tenant insurer for losses

exposure_statement.tenant: Insurance obligations incompletely defined; tenant may face uncovered losses and disputed coverage scope without a clear subrogation waiver
exposure_statement.landlord: Insurance obligations incompletely defined; landlord lacks reliable recourse against tenant insurers for premises-related losses and has no subrogation waiver to limit cross-claims
exposure_statement.neutral: Insurance requirements are incomplete; the missing waiver of subrogation leaves either party exposed to recovery actions by the other's insurer following a covered loss

negative_space_clues: Waiver of subrogation section present but obligation direction reversed or blank
Certificate delivery obligation cross-references deleted notice section
common_tenant_modifications: Reduced minimum coverage amounts
Removal of business interruption requirement
Mutual waiver of subrogation (one-way → two-way)

issue_areas.name: Subletting & Assignment
expected_elements: landlord consent requirement
grounds for withholding consent (reasonableness standard)
affiliate exception (no consent required for related entities)
profit sharing on sublet above base rent
recapture right (landlord can terminate and lease directly)
assignment in connection with sale of business

coverage_state_rules.missing: No assignment provision
coverage_state_rules.partial: Consent requirement present but affiliate exception, recapture, or profit sharing absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Landlord consent in sole and absolute discretion; no affiliate exception
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Affiliate defined by cross-reference to definition section not present in document

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Assignment rights undefined; tenant unable to sell business or transfer lease in routine transactions
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Assignment rights absent or over-restricted; tenant cannot execute routine business transactions including sale of business
negative_space_clues: Affiliate exception section marked Reserved
Sale-of-business exception cross-references deleted exhibit
common_tenant_modifications: Reasonableness standard added ('not unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed')
Affiliate exception broadened (parent, subsidiary, successor entities)
Sale-of-business exception expanded to include asset sales

issue_areas.name: Alterations & Improvements
expected_elements: threshold for required landlord approval (dollar amount or scope)
landlord contribution to tenant improvements (if any)
ownership of improvements at lease end
removal obligation at lease expiration
lien discharge or bond requirement

coverage_state_rules.missing: No alteration provision
coverage_state_rules.partial: Approval threshold present but removal obligation, ownership, or lien discharge absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Landlord may require removal of all tenant improvements at discretion
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Tenant improvement allowance cross-references Work Letter exhibit not attached

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Tenant may not make any alterations without implied landlord consent; improvements may revert to landlord

exposure_statement.tenant: Alteration rights undefined; tenant faces removal obligation uncertainty and potential forfeiture of improvement investment
exposure_statement.landlord: Tenant improvement allowance undefined; landlord faces uncertainty over its capital contribution exposure and the scope of improvements it may inherit at lease end
exposure_statement.neutral: Alteration rights and improvement-cost allocation are undefined; ownership and removal obligations for tenant-funded improvements at lease end are unresolved

negative_space_clues: Tenant improvement allowance section marked Reserved or amount is $0
Work Letter cross-referenced but exhibit absent from document
common_tenant_modifications: Approval threshold increased (above $10,000 or $25,000)
Removal obligation limited to trade fixtures only
Landlord required to designate removal items at time of approval

issue_areas.name: Default & Remedies
expected_elements: monetary default definition and cure period (typically 5 days)
non-monetary default definition and cure period (typically 30 days)
notice requirement before default declaration
landlord termination right
landlord re-entry right
tenant's right to cure third-party defaults
rent acceleration on default

coverage_state_rules.missing: No default provision
coverage_state_rules.partial: Monetary default present but non-monetary default, notice requirement, or cure period absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Cure period unusually short (under 30 days for non-monetary); OR landlord remedies aggressive but conditioned on prior notice and cure opportunity
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Remedies cross-reference deleted exhibit or section
coverage_state_rules.potentially_unenforceable: Self-help re-entry language permitting landlord to re-enter and remove tenant or property without judicial process AND without explicit reservation of tenant's right to legal process; covered_unfavorable governs when re-entry language is aggressive but conditioned on notice and cure

issue_areas.notes: Rule precedence v1.1.4: covered_unfavorable governs aggressive remedies that are still gated by notice/cure procedures. potentially_unenforceable is reserved for self-help language that bypasses judicial process entirely. When both could arguably apply, covered_unfavorable is the safer default; potentially_unenforceable should require explicit absence of legal-process reservation (e.g. clause states landlord 'may re-enter without legal process' or equivalent).
issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Landlord remedies limited to common law; no contractual right to accelerate rent or re-enter
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Default and remedy framework absent or incomplete; landlord enforcement position significantly weakened
negative_space_clues: Remedy section header present but acceleration clause absent
Notice requirement section marked Reserved
common_tenant_modifications: Extended cure periods (5 days → 10 days monetary; 30 days → 45 days non-monetary)
Notice required before every default declaration
Added third-party cure right (mortgagee or guarantor may cure)

issue_areas.name: Early Termination
exclusion_clues: no right to terminate prior to expiration
issue_areas.notes: Absence is normal and expected. Activation clues tightened v1.1.2 to prevent false positives on default/remedies language.
expected_elements: triggering conditions for early termination right
notice period required
termination fee or penalty formula
unamortized tenant improvement cost recovery
co-tenancy termination trigger (if applicable)

coverage_state_rules.missing: Termination right referenced elsewhere in lease but no termination provision found
coverage_state_rules.partial: Termination right exists but penalty formula, notice period, or survival obligations absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Termination fee includes unamortized brokerage commissions
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Termination fee formula cross-references amortization schedule exhibit not attached
coverage_state_rules.not_applicable: No termination right language anywhere in document; absence is by design

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Tenant has no exit mechanism; full remaining lease obligations survive business failure or relocation

exposure_statement.tenant: No early exit right; tenant bears full term obligation regardless of operational changes
exposure_statement.landlord: No tenant early termination right; landlord retains full-term revenue certainty but loses the ability to recapture and re-let the space if a better tenant emerges
exposure_statement.neutral: No early termination right is defined; full-term obligations persist unless another lease provision independently permits termination

negative_space_clues: Early termination section present but triggering conditions blank
Co-tenancy termination right cross-references anchor tenant definition not in document
common_tenant_modifications: Added termination right after Year 3 or Year 5
Termination fee capped at 6-12 months rent
Co-tenancy clause added (right to terminate if anchor tenant leaves)

issue_areas.name: Indemnification & Liability
expected_elements: tenant indemnification of landlord scope
landlord indemnification of tenant scope
mutual vs one-way indemnification structure
cap on liability (if any)
exclusion of consequential or punitive damages
carve-outs for indemnitee negligence

coverage_state_rules.missing: No indemnification provision
coverage_state_rules.partial: One-way indemnification present (tenant → landlord only) without reciprocal protection
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: No liability cap; consequential damages not excluded; OR mutual indemnification structurally present but materially asymmetric (e.g. tenant indemnifies for broad scope including ordinary negligence while landlord indemnification is limited to gross negligence or willful misconduct)
coverage_state_rules.potentially_unenforceable: Indemnification for indemnitee's own gross negligence

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Liability defaults to common law negligence standards
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Indemnification absent or one-sided; tenant bears uncapped liability exposure with no landlord reciprocal protection
negative_space_clues: Landlord indemnification section marked Reserved or deleted
Liability cap provision header present but amount blank
Landlord indemnification limited to gross negligence or willful misconduct while tenant indemnification covers ordinary negligence or all premises accidents
Tenant indemnifies for accidents 'in or about the Premises' regardless of cause without carve-out for landlord's own negligence
common_tenant_modifications: Added mutual/reciprocal indemnification
Added cap on total liability (typically 12-24 months rent)
Excluded consequential, punitive, and special damages

issue_areas.name: Force Majeure
issue_areas.notes: Cascade risk: definition expansions silently affect LP-05 continuous operation obligations. v1.1.3: Added partial-abatement expected_element and 'wholly untenantable only' pattern to covered_unfavorable rule.
expected_elements: definition of qualifying force majeure events
scope of excused obligations (which parties, which obligations)
rent abatement during force majeure period
partial rent abatement or adjustment for operational impairment
notice requirement to invoke
termination right if force majeure exceeds threshold period

coverage_state_rules.missing: No force majeure provision
coverage_state_rules.partial: Events defined but rent abatement, notice requirement, or termination right absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Abatement limited to 'wholly untenantable' standard with no partial abatement for operational impairment; OR tenant required to vacate to claim any abatement; OR force majeure excludes rent obligations entirely
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Force majeure definition includes catch-all language without enumeration

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: No excused performance; common law impossibility doctrine rarely applies to commercial leases
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Force majeure protection absent or limited to total untenantability; tenant may be obligated to pay full rent during partial operational impairment (utility loss, restricted access, regulatory shutdown, HVAC failure) that leaves premises legally occupiable but operationally unusable for the tenant's permitted business
negative_space_clues: Force majeure section present but rent abatement carve-out blank or deleted
Event list ends with 'including without limitation' with body truncated
Abatement available only if premises are 'wholly untenantable' with no partial-impairment mechanism
Abatement conditioned on tenant vacating the premises
common_tenant_modifications: Added pandemics, cyberattacks, supply chain disruptions to event list
Added rent abatement for force majeure periods exceeding 30 days
Added termination right if force majeure exceeds 180 days
Added partial abatement mechanism for operational impairment short of total untenantability

issue_areas.name: Signage Rights
exclusion_clues: tenant shall have no right to install signs
issue_areas.notes: Retail tenants almost always have signage rights.
expected_elements: exterior signage right (storefront/facade)
pylon or monument sign right
directory listing right
approval process and timeline
landlord's right to modify or remove
compliance with code and center standards

coverage_state_rules.missing: No signage provision in a retail lease
coverage_state_rules.partial: Storefront signage addressed but pylon, directory, or approval process absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Landlord may modify or remove signage at any time without notice
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Right to 'reasonable signage' without specification
coverage_state_rules.not_applicable: Non-retail context confirmed; signage not expected

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Tenant has no right to exterior signage; landlord can deny any brand identification at premises
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Signage rights undefined; tenant's brand visibility at premises unprotected and subject to landlord discretion
negative_space_clues: Signage specification cross-references Sign Criteria exhibit not attached
Pylon sign right granted but panel dimensions blank
common_tenant_modifications: Added pylon sign panel right
Minimum sign dimensions specified
Approval timeline specified (30 days; deemed approved if no response)

issue_areas.name: Parking
exclusion_clues: tenant is responsible for own parking
expected_elements: parking space allocation (count or ratio per square foot)
reserved vs unreserved designation
parking cost (included in rent or separately charged)
landlord's right to modify parking area
visitor / customer parking access
exclusive parking protection

coverage_state_rules.missing: Parking referenced in lease but no parking provision found
coverage_state_rules.partial: Spaces allocated but cost, reservation status, or modification rights absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Landlord may reduce parking allocation or convert to paid parking at any time
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Parking 'in common with other tenants' without space count or ratio

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: No contractual parking rights; landlord may charge for or eliminate parking access
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Parking rights undefined or unprotected; tenant customers and employees may face parking restrictions without recourse
negative_space_clues: Parking Exhibit referenced but not attached
Reserved space locations cross-reference site plan not included in document
common_tenant_modifications: Minimum space count guaranteed regardless of center reconfiguration
Cost of reserved spaces capped or included in base rent

issue_areas.name: Dispute Resolution
expected_elements: dispute resolution mechanism (mediation, arbitration, or litigation)
governing law (state)
venue / jurisdiction
attorney fee allocation (one-way or prevailing party)
jury trial waiver
time limit for bringing claims

coverage_state_rules.missing: No dispute resolution provision
coverage_state_rules.partial: Governing law present but venue, attorney fee allocation, or jury waiver absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Attorney fees one-way (landlord only); jury trial waived by tenant only
coverage_state_rules.potentially_unenforceable: Mandatory arbitration clause may be unenforceable against certain tenant types

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Dispute venue and cost allocation undefined; may favor party with greater litigation resources

exposure_statement.tenant: Dispute framework absent; attorney fee allocation and venue undefined, creating uncertainty in enforcement cost
exposure_statement.landlord: Dispute framework incomplete; attorney fee allocation and claim limitation periods undefined, creating uncertainty in landlord's enforcement leverage and defense costs
exposure_statement.neutral: Dispute framework is incomplete; the absence of a defined claims-limitation period and clear fee allocation leaves enforcement cost and timing exposure on both sides

negative_space_clues: Attorney fee allocation section blank or marked Reserved
Jury trial waiver section marked Intentionally Omitted
common_tenant_modifications: Prevailing party fee allocation made mutual (not landlord-only)
Jury trial waiver made mutual
Venue changed to tenant's county

issue_areas.name: Holdover Provisions
expected_elements: holdover rent rate (typically 150% of final month's rent)
month-to-month vs tenancy-at-sufferance characterization
notice required to terminate holdover
landlord's right to collect consequential damages from holdover
conversion to new lease conditions

coverage_state_rules.missing: No holdover provision; holdover tenancy governed by state law default
coverage_state_rules.partial: Holdover rate defined but notice requirement or tenancy characterization absent
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Holdover converts automatically to new 12-month term; consequential damages unlimited
coverage_state_rules.potentially_unenforceable: Holdover rate above 200% may be characterized as penalty clause

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Holdover defaults to state law; tenant may create new full-term tenancy by staying even one day past expiration
issue_areas.exposure_statement: Holdover protection undefined; tenant faces unlimited consequential damage exposure and potential automatic lease renewal
negative_space_clues: Holdover rate multiplier blank
Consequential damages section marked Reserved
common_tenant_modifications: Holdover rate reduced (200% → 150%)
Consequential damages excluded
Month-to-month characterization confirmed (prevents automatic term renewal)

issue_areas.name: Utilities
issue_areas.notes: Required in every commercial lease. Allocation may be tenant-direct (separately metered), pass-through via CAM (LP-07), or landlord-included in gross rent. All three structures are valid; absence of any utility provision is the gap.
expected_elements: identification of covered utilities (electric, gas, water, sewer, telecommunications, trash)
cost allocation method (tenant direct, separately metered, pass-through, or landlord-included)
submetering or check meter rights
responsibility for installation and connection costs
rent abatement or remedies for prolonged service interruption
responsibility for utility upgrade costs

coverage_state_rules.missing: No utility provision found
coverage_state_rules.partial: Cost allocation present but interruption remedies, upgrade cost responsibility, or submetering rights absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Utilities allocated to 'appropriate party' or 'as customary' without specification
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: No rent abatement for prolonged utility interruption; OR tenant bears all utility upgrade costs without cap; OR tenant required to pay for shared utility cost without submetering
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Utility allocation cross-references exhibit, schedule, or definition not present in document

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Utility cost allocation and service interruption rights undefined; tenant may face unexpected utility expenses or lose abatement rights during outages, particularly material for tenants with high utility dependency (food service, healthcare, refrigeration-dependent retail)

exposure_statement.tenant: Utility cost allocation and service interruption rights undefined; tenant may face unexpected utility expenses or lose rent abatement during prolonged outages, particularly material for operations dependent on continuous service
exposure_statement.landlord: Utility cost allocation and interruption remedies undefined; landlord may bear costs intended for tenant or face disputes over abatement obligations during third-party utility failures
exposure_statement.neutral: Utility cost allocation and service interruption rights are undefined; both parties face uncertainty over expense responsibility and abatement during outages

negative_space_clues: Utilities listed in lease summary but no allocation provision in body
'Tenant shall pay for all utilities' without submetering or check meter rights
Utility room or service entry referenced but tenant access rights not granted
Service interruption section header present but body blank or marked Reserved
Utility upgrade cost provision references exhibit not attached
common_tenant_modifications: Added rent abatement after 5 or 7 days of utility interruption
Submetering or check meter rights added
Utility upgrade costs allocated to landlord or capped
Cap on tenant's share of shared utility costs

issue_areas.name: Exclusivity
exclusion_clues: tenant has no exclusive use right
landlord retains right to lease to competitors
issue_areas.notes: Extracted from LP-05 in schema v1.2.0. Most retail leases include exclusivity for the tenant's primary business; absence is meaningful for retail tenants but normal for office or industrial tenants. Carve-outs swallow exclusivity if too broad — material question for any retail tenant whose competitive moat depends on this clause.
expected_elements: specific exclusive use scope (protected business activities defined precisely)
carve-outs for existing tenants at center
carve-outs for ancillary or incidental use by other tenants
radius restriction or geographic scope
definition of 'competing use'
remedies for landlord violation (rent abatement, damages, termination)
duration of exclusivity (full term or limited period)

coverage_state_rules.missing: Exclusive use referenced elsewhere in lease (e.g., recitals or LP-05) but no standalone exclusivity provision
coverage_state_rules.partial: Exclusive scope defined but remedies, carve-outs, or competing-use definition absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Exclusive use language without specific business definition, or 'reasonable' exclusivity without scope
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Carve-outs effectively swallow the exclusivity (e.g., grocery pharmacy carve-out for a pharmacy tenant); OR no remedies for landlord violation; OR landlord retains unilateral right to modify exclusivity
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Exclusive area or carve-out list cross-references exhibit not attached
coverage_state_rules.not_applicable: Document explicitly states no exclusivity, OR tenant type does not warrant exclusivity (office, industrial)

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Tenant has no protection from competing tenants at the center; landlord may lease adjacent space to direct competitors, eroding tenant's revenue base. Particularly material for retail tenants whose location-based competitive moat is the rationale for the lease

exposure_statement.tenant: Exclusivity protection absent or undefined; tenant has no contractual protection from competing tenants and no enforcement mechanism if landlord violates
exposure_statement.landlord: Exclusivity scope and carve-outs undefined; landlord faces potential disputes over what constitutes 'competing use' and may have leasing flexibility unintentionally constrained
exposure_statement.neutral: Exclusivity scope, carve-outs, and remedies are undefined; both parties face uncertainty over what competition is permitted at the center and what enforcement looks like if exclusivity is violated

negative_space_clues: Exclusive use clause header present but body blank or marked Reserved
Carve-outs section present but list blank
Reference to 'Exhibit C — Exclusive Use Area' or similar with no exhibit attached
Definition of 'competing use' absent from Definitions article
Remedies section blank or limited to 'landlord shall use commercially reasonable efforts'
Radius restriction percentage or distance blank
common_tenant_modifications: Added remedies for violation (rent abatement, termination right after notice and cure)
Tightened definition of 'competing use' to specific SIC/NAICS codes
Limited carve-outs (no general grocery exception for pharmacy tenant)
Added radius restriction (e.g., no competing use within 1 mile)
Extended exclusivity for full lease term including renewal options

issue_areas.name: Guaranty of Lease
exclusion_clues: no personal guarantee shall be required
issue_areas.notes: Promoted from discovered_provision_patterns in schema v1.2.0. Common for newer tenants, smaller tenants, single-purpose entity tenants, or where landlord requires additional credit support beyond the security deposit. Absence is normal for established/creditworthy tenants and not a flag.
expected_elements: identification of guarantor (individual or entity, with address)
scope of guaranteed obligations (rent only, all lease obligations, or specified subset)
guaranty type (full, limited, good guy, burndown)
recourse mechanism (direct action against guarantor, or after exhausting tenant remedies)
duration of guaranty (full lease term, defined period, or until release conditions met)
release conditions (sale of business, hitting financial milestones, vacate and pay obligations met)
survival of guaranty after lease assignment or modification

coverage_state_rules.missing: Guaranty referenced in recitals, signature block, or other lease provisions but no guaranty article or attached guaranty agreement found
coverage_state_rules.partial: Guarantor identified but scope, duration, type, or release conditions absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Guaranty type unclear (full vs limited not specified); OR 'good guy guaranty' invoked without definition
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Guaranty extends beyond lease term with no termination mechanism; OR guarantor remains liable after release of tenant; OR no release conditions defined; OR 'all obligations forever' language without limitation
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Lease references separate Guaranty Agreement attached as exhibit but exhibit not present in document
coverage_state_rules.potentially_unenforceable: Guaranty not signed by guarantor; OR notarization required by jurisdiction not present; OR guaranty waives statutory protections that may not be waivable
coverage_state_rules.not_applicable: No guaranty references anywhere in document; tenant alone is responsible

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: If a guaranty was negotiated, landlord has no enforceable third-party recourse if tenant defaults; landlord's credit position is limited to tenant entity assets and the security deposit

exposure_statement.tenant: Guaranty terms incompletely defined; guarantor's scope, duration, and release conditions undefined, creating uncertainty about personal exposure and inability to plan exit from guaranty obligation
exposure_statement.landlord: Guaranty terms incompletely defined; landlord lacks clear enforcement mechanism against guarantor, faces uncertainty over guaranty survival across lease modifications, and may have weakened credit support if guaranty is unenforceable
exposure_statement.neutral: Guaranty terms, scope, recourse, duration, and release conditions are undefined; both parties face uncertainty over the third-party backstop's enforceability and how it interacts with lease modifications or assignment

negative_space_clues: Signature block lists guarantor but no guaranty article in lease body
Recitals or lease summary references guaranty but provision absent
'Good guy guaranty' invoked without definition
Burndown schedule referenced but timing and triggers blank
Release conditions section header present but body blank or marked Reserved
Reference to separate Guaranty Agreement exhibit not attached
Guarantor signature line present but unsigned
common_tenant_modifications: Good guy guaranty (personal liability ends when tenant vacates and pays through vacate date)
Burndown schedule (guaranty amount reduces over time as tenant performs)
Release on financial milestones (revenue, net worth, or operating history thresholds)
Cap on guaranty amount (e.g., 12 months rent maximum exposure)
Release on assignment of lease to qualified assignee
Limited guaranty scope (rent only, not all lease obligations)

issue_areas.name: SNDA (Subordination, Non-Disturbance & Attornment)
issue_areas.notes: Promoted from discovered_provision_patterns in schema v1.3.0. Critical for tenant protection when landlord has or may obtain financing secured by the property. Without a non-disturbance agreement, tenant's lease may be extinguished on landlord foreclosure. Common in institutional retail and any property with a mortgage.
expected_elements: subordination of lease to senior mortgage or deed of trust
non-disturbance covenant from lender (lease survives foreclosure if tenant not in default)
attornment obligation (tenant recognizes successor landlord after foreclosure)
form of SNDA (landlord-prepared, tenant approval right, or recognized form)
lender obligation to execute SNDA within defined period
survival and binding effect on successors and assigns

coverage_state_rules.missing: SNDA referenced in lease or recitals but no SNDA provision or exhibit found
coverage_state_rules.partial: Subordination or attornment present but non-disturbance covenant absent; OR SNDA form referenced but not attached
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Lease states it is subject to mortgage but SNDA terms not defined
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Non-disturbance limited to specific events or conditioned on lender approval at time of foreclosure; OR SNDA form is lender's standard form with no tenant modification right; OR no obligation on lender to execute within defined period
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: SNDA referenced as Exhibit or separate agreement but not attached to document
coverage_state_rules.not_applicable: Property described as unencumbered and no mortgage referenced anywhere in document

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Tenant's lease may be extinguished on landlord's lender foreclosure; tenant loses occupancy right and all leasehold improvements without compensation regardless of default status

exposure_statement.tenant: Non-disturbance protection absent; tenant's leasehold rights may be extinguished if landlord's lender forecloses, regardless of whether tenant is in default
exposure_statement.landlord: SNDA terms undefined; landlord may be unable to obtain financing without tenant cooperation, and successor landlord's obligations to existing tenants are uncertain
exposure_statement.neutral: SNDA terms, non-disturbance scope, and attornment conditions are undefined; both parties face uncertainty over the lease's survival through a lender foreclosure

negative_space_clues: Lease recitals reference existing mortgage but no SNDA article
Subordination clause present but non-disturbance absent
SNDA Exhibit placeholder present but exhibit not attached
Lender consent required for assignment but no SNDA addresses lender's obligations to tenant
Estoppel certificate obligation references SNDA but no SNDA found
common_tenant_modifications: Non-disturbance covenant added (key negotiating point — landlord often resists)
Lender SNDA form subject to tenant's reasonable approval
Lender required to execute SNDA within 30 days of tenant's written request
SNDA extends to all future mortgages, not just existing encumbrances
Lender bound by all landlord obligations under the lease after foreclosure

issue_areas.name: Percentage Rent
exclusion_clues: rent is not based on sales
issue_areas.notes: Promoted from discovered_provision_patterns in schema v1.3.0. Common in retail leases, particularly for food service, soft goods, and high-traffic retail. The calculation methodology and gross sales definition are the primary dispute vectors — broad gross sales definitions favor landlord; broad exclusions favor tenant.
expected_elements: gross sales definition (what is included and excluded)
percentage rate applied to gross sales above breakpoint
natural or artificial breakpoint (base rent / percentage rate, or defined dollar amount)
reporting period and frequency (monthly, quarterly, or annual)
deadline for annual reconciliation statement
landlord audit rights over gross sales records
exclusions from gross sales (returns, exchanges, sales taxes, credit card fees)

coverage_state_rules.missing: Percentage rent referenced in base economics but no percentage rent article found
coverage_state_rules.partial: Percentage rate and breakpoint defined but gross sales definition, reporting obligations, or audit rights absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Percentage rent described generally without defined rate, breakpoint, or gross sales definition
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Gross sales definition includes sales made outside premises or internet sales; OR no exclusion for sales tax or credit card processing fees; OR audit rights absent or limited to 12 months; OR landlord may estimate gross sales if tenant fails to report
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Gross sales definition or breakpoint calculation references exhibit not attached

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Percentage rent obligations unenforceable or undefined; landlord cannot collect overage rent and tenant has no clear reporting or recordkeeping obligations

exposure_statement.tenant: Percentage rent calculation, gross sales definition, and audit exposure are undefined; tenant may face disputed overage rent claims or be unable to limit gross sales inclusions
exposure_statement.landlord: Percentage rent calculation and reporting obligations undefined; landlord cannot reliably collect overage rent or audit tenant's sales records
exposure_statement.neutral: Percentage rent rate, breakpoint, gross sales definition, and audit rights are undefined; both parties face uncertainty over overage rent obligations and verification rights

negative_space_clues: Lease summary shows percentage rate and breakpoint but no percentage rent article in body
Annual reconciliation deadline blank
Gross sales definition absent from Definitions article
Audit rights section header present but body blank or marked Reserved
Reporting schedule references exhibit not attached
common_tenant_modifications: Broad gross sales exclusions (online sales, catering, wholesale, gift cards)
Credit card processing fees excluded from gross sales
Artificial breakpoint set higher than natural breakpoint
Audit window limited to 2 years; findings deemed final if not contested
Annual gross sales cap after which no further percentage rent is owed

issue_areas.name: Damage & Destruction
issue_areas.notes: Required in every commercial lease. The landlord repair deadline and tenant's termination right are the key negotiating points — landlord wants maximum time and minimum termination exposure; tenant wants a hard deadline with a clean termination right. The 'total loss' threshold determines which party can exit.
expected_elements: landlord's obligation to repair or rebuild following insured casualty
rent abatement during period of repair (full vs. partial based on usability)
landlord repair deadline (often 180-270 days from damage with architect certification)
tenant's right to terminate if repairs not completed within defined period
landlord's right to terminate if damage occurs near end of term or is uninsurable
definition of total loss or destruction threshold
disposition of insurance proceeds if lease terminates

coverage_state_rules.missing: No damage and destruction provision found
coverage_state_rules.partial: Repair obligation present but repair deadline, abatement scope, or termination right absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Landlord obligated to repair 'as soon as practicable' without defined deadline or termination right
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: No rent abatement during repair period; OR landlord's repair deadline so long (>270 days) as to render tenant's termination right illusory; OR landlord retains right to terminate on any casualty without rebuilding; OR tenant bears cost of rebuilding tenant improvements above insurance proceeds
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Damage & destruction provision cross-references insurance exhibit or architect certification procedure not present in document

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: If premises are damaged, tenant has no guaranteed right to rent abatement, no landlord repair obligation, no termination right if repairs are never completed, and no clarity on insurance proceeds disposition

exposure_statement.tenant: Damage and destruction obligations are undefined; tenant may be required to pay full rent on unusable premises, have no termination right if landlord fails to rebuild, and no clarity on insurance proceeds if the lease terminates
exposure_statement.landlord: Damage and destruction obligations are undefined; landlord faces uncertain repair obligations, dispute over insurance proceeds allocation, and potential tenant claims for abatement without a defined framework
exposure_statement.neutral: Damage and destruction repair obligations, abatement rights, termination triggers, and insurance proceeds disposition are undefined; both parties face significant uncertainty following a casualty event

negative_space_clues: Casualty insurance required but no damage and destruction provision in lease body
Damage and destruction section header present but body blank or marked Reserved
Repair deadline blank in damage and destruction clause
Insurance proceeds allocation provision references separate agreement not attached
Force majeure provision references damage and destruction but no separate article found
common_tenant_modifications: Hard landlord repair deadline (180 days) with architect certification of completion
Tenant termination right if repairs exceed 180-270 days or are not commenced within 60 days
Full rent abatement during repair period (not just proportionate to unusable portion)
Tenant rebuild allowance for tenant improvements above base building insurance
Tenant right to terminate if damage occurs in last 12-18 months of term

issue_areas.name: Condemnation / Eminent Domain
issue_areas.notes: Required in every commercial lease. Often treated as a companion to the damage and destruction provision. The allocation of condemnation awards — particularly tenant's right to a separate award for trade fixtures, leasehold improvements, and business losses — is the primary negotiating point.
expected_elements: definition of total taking vs. material partial taking
lease termination right on total taking or material partial taking
rent abatement or reduction on partial taking proportionate to loss of premises
allocation of condemnation award between landlord and tenant
tenant's right to separate award for trade fixtures, leasehold improvements, moving costs, and business losses
restoration obligation if lease continues after partial taking
definition of 'material' partial taking (e.g., loss of parking, access, or defined percentage of floor area)

coverage_state_rules.missing: No condemnation or eminent domain provision found
coverage_state_rules.partial: Termination right on total taking present but partial taking treatment, award allocation, or restoration obligation absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: General condemnation clause without definition of material partial taking or tenant award entitlement
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Landlord entitled to entire condemnation award including value of leasehold; OR tenant has no termination right on partial taking that destroys utility of premises; OR no restoration obligation after partial taking
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Condemnation award allocation or restoration procedure cross-references exhibit not attached

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: On condemnation, tenant has no guaranteed right to share in the award, no termination right if partial taking renders premises unusable, and no rent reduction right — all defaults to state law which may be unfavorable

exposure_statement.tenant: Condemnation rights are undefined; tenant may receive no portion of the condemnation award, have no termination right on material partial taking, and face full rent obligation on diminished premises
exposure_statement.landlord: Condemnation provisions are undefined; landlord faces uncertain obligations to restore, reduce rent, or allow termination after a partial taking, with increased dispute exposure
exposure_statement.neutral: Condemnation termination triggers, award allocation, and restoration obligations are undefined; both parties face significant uncertainty on a government taking of all or part of the premises

negative_space_clues: Eminent domain or condemnation section header present but body blank or marked Reserved
Lease summary references condemnation but no article in lease body
Award allocation provision references separate agreement not attached
Definition of 'material partial taking' blank or omitted from Definitions article
common_tenant_modifications: Tenant entitled to separate award for trade fixtures, leasehold improvements, and moving costs
Tenant termination right on partial taking that reduces usable floor area by defined percentage (e.g., 15%) or eliminates parking access
Rent reduction proportionate to loss of premises area following partial taking
Landlord restoration obligation if lease continues after partial taking
Business interruption damages excluded from landlord's award

issue_areas.name: Quiet Enjoyment
issue_areas.notes: Required in every commercial lease. A fundamental landlord covenant — its absence may be supplied by state law in many jurisdictions, but an express covenant is preferred to avoid jurisdictional ambiguity. The covenant should survive against lenders and successors for SNDA compatibility.
expected_elements: express quiet enjoyment covenant by landlord
covenant conditioned on tenant's performance of lease obligations (not absolute)
survival and binding effect on landlord's successors, assigns, and lenders
covenant not subject to any undisclosed superior lien or encumbrance

coverage_state_rules.missing: No quiet enjoyment covenant found; tenant relies solely on state law implied covenant
coverage_state_rules.partial: Quiet enjoyment clause present but not conditioned on tenant performance OR does not bind successors and lenders
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Quiet enjoyment referenced without definition of scope or conditions
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Covenant is conditioned on landlord's receipt of rent from tenant rather than tenant's compliance with all lease obligations; OR covenant explicitly does not bind lenders or successors in interest
coverage_state_rules.potentially_unenforceable: Quiet enjoyment covenant purports to be absolute (not conditioned on tenant's performance) — may conflict with landlord's right to re-enter on tenant default

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Tenant's right to undisturbed possession depends on state law implied covenant, which varies by jurisdiction and may be narrower than an express covenant; particularly material if property is mortgaged and SNDA does not independently protect tenant

exposure_statement.tenant: Quiet enjoyment covenant absent or undefined; tenant's right to undisturbed possession depends on state law, which varies and may not protect against lender interference
exposure_statement.landlord: Quiet enjoyment covenant undefined; landlord faces uncertainty over scope of obligation and whether covenant binds successors, creating potential dispute on transfer or financing
exposure_statement.neutral: Quiet enjoyment scope, conditions, and survival against successors and lenders are undefined; both parties face uncertainty over tenant's right to undisturbed possession

negative_space_clues: Quiet enjoyment referenced in recitals or lease summary but no covenant in lease body
SNDA provision present but quiet enjoyment covenant absent
Landlord's representations section blank or marked Reserved
common_tenant_modifications: Covenant confirmed to bind lenders and mortgagees (coordinates with SNDA)
Absolute covenant for initial term (no conditioned-on-tenant-performance qualifier)
Explicit statement that landlord's right to re-enter does not breach quiet enjoyment covenant

issue_areas.name: Landlord Default & Tenant Remedies
issue_areas.notes: The counterpart to LP-11 (tenant default). Often conspicuously weaker or absent in landlord-form leases — landlords frequently attempt to limit tenant remedies to specific performance only, eliminating offset rights, self-help rights, and termination rights. The tenant's ability to offset rent against uncured landlord obligations is a major negotiating point.
expected_elements: definition of landlord default events (failure to perform material obligations after notice and cure)
notice and cure period before tenant may exercise remedies (typically 30 days written + additional reasonable time for complex repairs)
tenant self-help right to cure at landlord's expense after cure period expires
rent offset right against verified self-help costs
tenant's right to terminate on material uncured landlord default
lender third-party cure right (lender may cure landlord default within additional cure period)
limitation on landlord's personal liability (typically limited to interest in the property)

coverage_state_rules.missing: No landlord default provision found; tenant's remedies limited to state law defaults
coverage_state_rules.partial: Landlord default defined but self-help right, offset right, or termination right absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Landlord default clause present but remedies described as 'tenant's rights at law and equity' without enumeration
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Tenant remedy limited to specific performance only (no termination, no offset, no self-help); OR notice and cure period so long as to render remedies impractical; OR landlord default provision explicitly excludes rent offset right
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Landlord default cure procedure cross-references notice article or lender SNDA not present in document

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: On landlord's failure to perform (e.g., failure to maintain HVAC, roof, or common areas), tenant has no clear self-help right, no rent offset, and may be unable to terminate — all remedies default to litigation, which is slow and expensive

exposure_statement.tenant: Landlord default remedies undefined; tenant has no self-help right, no rent offset, and may be unable to terminate if landlord fails to maintain the premises or perform material obligations
exposure_statement.landlord: Landlord default terms undefined; landlord faces uncertainty over cure period and exposure to tenant self-help costs or termination claims without a defined notice-and-cure framework
exposure_statement.neutral: Landlord default events, cure periods, and tenant remedies are undefined; both parties face uncertainty over what constitutes a material landlord breach and what remedies are available

negative_space_clues: Tenant default section detailed but landlord default section absent or one sentence
Landlord default section header present but body blank or marked Reserved
Tenant remedies limited to 'rights at law' without enumeration
Self-help provision referenced in another article but no landlord default article found
SNDA requires lender cure right but no landlord default article defines what is being cured
common_tenant_modifications: Self-help right added: tenant may cure after 30-day notice + additional reasonable time
Rent offset right against verified self-help costs (limited to 2-3 months rent per event)
Termination right after material uncured default exceeding 90 days
Lender cure period limited to additional 30 days after landlord's cure period expires
Landlord liability not limited to property interest for fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence

issue_areas.name: Compliance with Laws
issue_areas.notes: Required in every commercial lease. The primary dispute vectors are ADA compliance cost allocation (structural ADA falls to landlord; tenant-use-specific ADA falls to tenant) and future law compliance (changes in law during the term that require expensive retrofits). Tenant should push to limit compliance obligations to those triggered by tenant's specific use.
expected_elements: tenant's obligation to comply with applicable laws, codes, and regulations in connection with tenant's use
landlord's obligation to deliver premises in compliance with applicable laws at commencement
allocation of structural vs. use-specific compliance costs
ADA compliance allocation (structural = landlord; ADA modifications for tenant's specific operations = tenant)
future changes in law during the term (who bears the cost of code changes not triggered by tenant's use)
grandfathering for pre-existing non-compliant conditions at lease commencement

coverage_state_rules.missing: No compliance with laws provision found
coverage_state_rules.partial: General compliance obligation present but cost allocation, ADA responsibility, or future-law treatment absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Compliance obligation stated without distinguishing between tenant-use-triggered and structural/code compliance costs
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Tenant required to comply with all laws including structural requirements regardless of trigger; OR tenant bears cost of future law compliance not triggered by tenant's specific use; OR no grandfathering for pre-existing non-compliant conditions
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Compliance obligation cross-references laws schedule or permitted-use exhibit not attached

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Tenant may be required to fund expensive structural compliance (ADA ramps, fire suppression upgrades) that should be landlord's responsibility, and may face uncapped exposure to future code changes during the lease term

exposure_statement.tenant: Compliance with laws obligations are undefined; tenant may face liability for structural or pre-existing non-compliance, uncapped future code change costs, and ADA upgrade obligations not triggered by tenant's specific use
exposure_statement.landlord: Compliance with laws obligations are undefined; landlord may face tenant claims for reimbursement of compliance costs that should have been landlord's responsibility under a properly allocated lease
exposure_statement.neutral: Compliance cost allocation, ADA responsibility, and future-law treatment are undefined; both parties face uncertainty over who bears the cost of legal compliance changes during the lease term

negative_space_clues: Compliance with laws section header present but body blank or marked Reserved
ADA defined in Definitions article but not addressed in compliance provision
Tenant's permitted use triggers specific regulatory requirements not addressed in compliance clause
Structural compliance referenced in tenant's obligations without landlord carve-out
common_tenant_modifications: Tenant compliance limited to laws triggered by tenant's specific use (not all laws)
Landlord responsible for structural compliance and ADA baseline requirements
Grandfathering: tenant not responsible for pre-existing non-compliant conditions at commencement
Future law compliance costs above defined threshold allocated to landlord
Landlord representation that premises comply with all applicable laws at commencement

issue_areas.name: Right of Entry / Landlord Access
issue_areas.notes: Required in every commercial lease. The notice period and permitted purposes for access are the primary negotiating points. Insufficient notice or unlimited access purposes can interfere with tenant's business operations.
expected_elements: notice period required before entry (standard: 24-48 hours prior written or verbal notice)
permitted purposes for entry (inspection, repair, showing to prospective tenants/buyers, emergency)
emergency entry without advance notice (limited to life-safety emergencies)
tenant's right to have representative present during non-emergency entry
restriction on entry frequency or timing (no entry during business hours without consent, or limited to defined hours)
landlord's obligation to minimize interference with tenant's business operations

coverage_state_rules.missing: No right of entry provision found; access governed by state law defaults only
coverage_state_rules.partial: Entry right defined but notice period, permitted purposes, or emergency entry limitation absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Entry permitted 'at reasonable times' without defined notice period or purpose limitation
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: No notice required for any entry (not just emergencies); OR unlimited entry purposes including showing to competitors; OR no obligation to minimize interference with tenant's business; OR tenant's representative right absent
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Entry notice procedure cross-references notice article not found in document

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Landlord may enter premises without notice, at any time, for any purpose — disrupting tenant's business operations, exposing confidential business information, and interfering with customers

exposure_statement.tenant: Landlord access terms undefined; landlord may enter without notice at any time, disrupting business operations, exposing confidential information, and interfering with customers
exposure_statement.landlord: Landlord access terms undefined; landlord faces uncertain rights to inspect, maintain, and show the property without a defined notice and entry framework
exposure_statement.neutral: Landlord entry notice requirements, permitted purposes, and frequency limitations are undefined; both parties face uncertainty over access rights and interference with business operations

negative_space_clues: Landlord's repair obligation present but no corresponding entry right or notice procedure
Showing rights during last year of term referenced but no general entry article found
Notice article references landlord's right of entry but no entry article exists
Emergency entry right asserted without definition of 'emergency'
common_tenant_modifications: 48-hour advance notice required except for life-safety emergencies
Entry only during normal business hours (9am-5pm weekdays) without tenant consent
Tenant's representative right during all non-emergency entries
Landlord's minimization of business interference obligation
Showing rights limited to last 12 months of term and with tenant representative present

issue_areas.name: Estoppel Certificate
activation_clues: confirm the status of the lease
exclusion_clues: tenant shall not be required to certify
issue_areas.notes: Common in institutional retail leases where landlord may seek financing or sell the property. Tenant's obligation to provide accurate estoppels is important but should be limited in frequency and form to avoid overreach.
expected_elements: tenant's obligation to provide estoppel certificate on landlord's written request
response deadline (typically 10-20 business days from request)
form of certificate (landlord-prepared form with tenant right to note exceptions)
scope of certification (lease status, rent payment current, no landlord default known, amendments listed)
consequence of failure to respond timely (deemed approval is common but problematic for tenant)
limitation on request frequency (maximum number per year, e.g., 2)

coverage_state_rules.missing: Estoppel certificate obligation referenced in lease economics or recitals but no article found
coverage_state_rules.partial: Estoppel obligation present but response deadline, frequency limit, or form approval right absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Estoppel obligation stated without defining content, form, or timeline
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Failure to respond within deadline deemed conclusive admission that no landlord defaults exist; OR no frequency limit on requests; OR tenant must certify beyond actual knowledge; OR form prepared solely by landlord with no tenant exception right
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Estoppel form referenced as exhibit but not attached to lease

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: If landlord cannot obtain tenant estoppels for a sale or financing, landlord may claim tenant breach; conversely, an uncontrolled estoppel obligation may require tenant to certify statements that later prove inaccurate

exposure_statement.tenant: Estoppel certificate terms undefined; tenant faces uncertainty over required scope of certification, liability for inaccurate statements, and deemed-approval traps if response obligations are not clearly limited
exposure_statement.landlord: Estoppel certificate procedure undefined; landlord may be unable to efficiently obtain tenant certifications needed for financing or property sale transactions
exposure_statement.neutral: Estoppel certificate scope, timing, deemed-approval consequences, and frequency limits are undefined; both parties face uncertainty over tenant's certification obligations and exposure

negative_space_clues: SNDA references estoppel but no estoppel article found
Estoppel form referenced as exhibit but exhibit not attached
Lease table of contents lists estoppel article but article body is blank or Reserved
Assignment approval procedure requires estoppel but no estoppel article defines procedure
common_tenant_modifications: Response deadline extended to 15-20 business days
No deemed-approval provision (failure to respond is not a concession)
Frequency limited to 2 requests per calendar year
Tenant certifies only to actual knowledge (not constructive or imputed knowledge)
Tenant may note exceptions to landlord's form estoppel rather than sign as prepared

issue_areas.name: Co-Tenancy
issue_areas.notes: Promoted from discovered_provision_patterns in schema v1.3.0. Significant for retail tenants whose traffic and sales depend on anchor tenants. Two types: opening co-tenancy (anchor must be open before tenant is required to open) and ongoing co-tenancy (anchor must continue operating). Both trigger rent modification or termination rights on failure.
expected_elements: opening co-tenancy condition (named anchor tenant(s) open and operating before tenant opening obligation)
ongoing co-tenancy condition (anchor tenant(s) continue operating or minimum occupancy threshold maintained)
remedy during co-tenancy failure period (typically reduced rent or percentage-rent-only mode)
cure period before remedy activates (typically 60-180 days after anchor closure)
termination right if co-tenancy failure continues beyond defined period (typically 12-24 months)
definition of 'anchor tenant' or minimum occupancy percentage threshold

coverage_state_rules.missing: Co-tenancy referenced in lease economics or recitals but no co-tenancy provision found in body
coverage_state_rules.partial: Co-tenancy condition defined but remedy, cure period, or termination right absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Co-tenancy referenced without defining anchor tenant, occupancy threshold, or applicable remedy
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Remedy during co-tenancy failure is merely percentage rent (no fixed floor); OR termination right not available until after extended co-tenancy failure period exceeding 24 months; OR definition of anchor tenant so broad that replacement tenant of any kind satisfies co-tenancy condition
coverage_state_rules.not_applicable: Document explicitly states no co-tenancy rights, OR lease type (office, industrial) where co-tenancy is not market standard

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Tenant may be required to pay full rent and remain open even if the center's anchor tenant closes and foot traffic collapses, with no rent reduction right and no exit strategy

exposure_statement.tenant: Co-tenancy protection absent or undefined; tenant may be required to pay full rent and remain open even if anchor tenants close and the center's viability materially deteriorates
exposure_statement.landlord: Co-tenancy terms undefined; landlord faces uncertain obligations to remedy anchor closures and may face tenant claims for unauthorized rent reduction
exposure_statement.neutral: Co-tenancy conditions, remedies, cure periods, and termination rights are undefined; both parties face uncertainty over tenant obligations during center anchor vacancies

negative_space_clues: Anchor tenant named in recitals but no co-tenancy article in lease body
Co-tenancy section header present but body blank or marked Reserved
Minimum occupancy threshold blank in co-tenancy clause
Termination right referenced in co-tenancy clause with blank cure period or trigger date
Lease summary shows co-tenancy condition but no governing provision found
common_tenant_modifications: Named anchor tenant(s) listed with obligation to reopen within 12 months if closed
Ongoing minimum occupancy threshold defined (e.g., 75% of GLA occupied by non-anchor tenants)
Remedy: fixed reduced rent (e.g., lesser of percentage rent or 50% of base rent) during failure
Termination right after 12 months of continuous co-tenancy failure
Replacement anchor standard tightened (replacement must be national brand or defined credit quality)

issue_areas.name: Hazardous Materials
exclusion_clues: tenant's use involves no hazardous materials
issue_areas.notes: Promoted from discovered_provision_patterns in schema v1.3.0. Highly jurisdiction-sensitive. The primary dispute vectors are the scope of prohibited substances (particularly for food service, medical, dry cleaning, and gas station tenants), the carve-out for ordinary course materials, and remediation cost allocation for pre-existing contamination.
expected_elements: definition of hazardous materials (by reference to CERCLA, RCRA, applicable state law, or enumeration)
carve-out for de minimis quantities of customary business materials (cleaning supplies, office materials, fuel for vehicles)
prohibition on use, storage, or disposal of hazardous materials except as permitted
tenant's remediation obligation at tenant's sole cost if contamination caused by tenant
landlord's representations on pre-existing contamination at commencement
tenant's right to conduct environmental testing if contamination suspected
notification requirement on release or discovery of hazardous condition
survival of hazardous materials obligations after lease expiration

coverage_state_rules.missing: No hazardous materials provision found in lease; environmental obligations governed by applicable law only
coverage_state_rules.partial: General hazardous materials prohibition present but carve-out for ordinary business materials, pre-existing contamination representations, or remediation allocation absent
coverage_state_rules.ambiguous: Hazardous materials referenced without definition or reference to applicable law; scope of prohibition unclear
coverage_state_rules.covered_unfavorable: Tenant required to remediate pre-existing contamination not caused by tenant; OR carve-out for ordinary business materials absent or too narrow for tenant's permitted use; OR tenant required to indemnify landlord for all environmental claims regardless of cause
coverage_state_rules.broken_xref: Hazardous materials exhibit, environmental baseline report, or permitted substances schedule referenced but not attached
coverage_state_rules.potentially_unenforceable: Tenant required to waive CERCLA or RCRA statutory rights in a manner that may not be permitted by applicable law

issue_areas.risk_if_missing: Tenant faces unlimited environmental liability without a defined scope of prohibited substances, carve-out for ordinary business materials, or protection against pre-existing contamination — particularly material for food service, medical, and chemical-dependent tenants

exposure_statement.tenant: Hazardous materials obligations are undefined; tenant may face liability for pre-existing contamination, have no carve-out for ordinary business materials, and face uncapped remediation costs for conditions not caused by tenant
exposure_statement.landlord: Hazardous materials obligations are undefined; landlord has no clear framework for monitoring tenant environmental compliance, allocating pre-existing contamination costs, or enforcing notification obligations
exposure_statement.neutral: Hazardous materials scope, permitted substances, pre-existing contamination allocation, and remediation obligations are undefined; both parties face significant uncertainty over environmental liability during and after the lease term

negative_space_clues: Tenant's permitted use involves food service, medical, dry cleaning, or chemicals but no hazardous materials provision found
Environmental indemnification in lease but no hazardous materials definition or carve-out
Hazardous materials section header present but body blank or marked Reserved
Environmental baseline report referenced in lease but not attached as exhibit
Permitted substances schedule referenced but not attached
common_tenant_modifications: Carve-out for ordinary course business materials in commercially reasonable quantities
Landlord representations on pre-existing contamination with indemnification for pre-lease conditions
Tenant remediation obligation limited to contamination caused or exacerbated by tenant
Tenant right to conduct Phase I/II environmental assessment at commencement
Notification right (not obligation) for third-party environmental claims not caused by tenant

discovered_provision_patterns.description: Common non-standard provisions discovered in tenant leases during CAM analysis (CUSTOM-XX entries).

patterns.name: Radius Restriction
patterns.coverage_concern: Restriction on tenant operating competing locations within defined radius

patterns.name: Relocation
patterns.coverage_concern: Landlord's right to relocate tenant to different premises

patterns.name: Continuous Operations
patterns.coverage_concern: Obligation to remain open and operating specific hours; penalties for going dark

schema_validation_rules.description: Rules for validating this schema file.
checks: every conditional issue_area has at least one activation_clue
every issue_area has at least one expected_element
coverage_state_rules reference only valid coverage states from coverage_states dict
caution_signals reference only valid keys from caution_signal_definitions
every discovered_provision_pattern has applicability and activation_clues
